evidence.claim: Equifax offers a Verification of Education Suite for verifying college enrollment, graduation, and degree information; this supports Equifax as a large-cap adjacent verification anchor not included in the four-name candidate list.

memory_update.text: PSO/Pearson should remain the reference leader for digital credentialing because Credly provides direct verified-skills and credential-network exposure.

FA/First Advantage is the best underfollowed mid-cap candidate found in this pass: education exposure is hidden inside background screening, credential verification, identity, ATS/HCM integrations, and hiring compliance workflows.
COUR/Coursera should be tracked not only as online learning but also as a proprietary skills-signal and microcredential data asset; verify monetization beyond enrollment.

SKIL/Skillsoft is a below-$300M speculative exception with direct skills-management language; survival depends on balance sheet, customer adoption, and whether Percipio skills data creates defensible recurring revenue.

Equifax was not included due to the four-candidate limit and large-cap status, but its Work Number and Verification of Education products make it an important large-cap adjacent verification anchor for later comparison.

The chokepoint may not be course delivery; it may be trusted verification rails and interoperable skills data connecting transcripts, badges, licenses, employment history, ATS/HCM systems, and workforce planning.

node: Skills data, credential verification, labor-market analytics, and learner records
summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around the skills-data and credential-verification node. The strongest reference anchor found is Pearson/Credly, because Credly directly issues and verifies digital credentials at network scale. The underfollowed lane is more interesting in background screening and enterprise skills-management vendors: First Advantage is not usually mapped as an education stock, but it touches education, employment, license, and credential verification inside hiring workflows; Skillsoft is a micro-cap speculative exception with direct enterprise skills-data exposure through Percipio; Coursera is more obvious as edtech but may be underappreciated as a skills-signal and microcredential data asset rather than only a course marketplace. No buy/sell view is implied.
